sections.heading: Frequently asked questions

items.question: What do I need to run my first search?
items.answer: Start with the kind of company you want, a geography, and the characteristics that make it a good fit. For example, landscapers in California that offer commercial snow removal.

items.question: Can it find companies that match my specific criteria?
items.answer: Describe what a business actually does, then use Signals to check the criteria that matter to you. Acquisition searchers can describe their thesis too, but a matching company does not mean its owner wants to sell.

items.question: How do I check whether the research is right?
items.answer: Review the source behind a finding before acting on it. Missing information should remain unknown rather than be treated as a confirmed match.

items.question: What does Scorecard tell me about a company?
items.answer: What it does, who it serves, how long it has operated and who runs it, with a source for each finding. Private-company revenue and willingness to sell may be unknown.

items.question: Can I export my results?
items.answer: Yes. Download your research as a CSV for your spreadsheet or CRM. Direct CRM integration is coming soon.

items.question: What’s included in the trial, and what happens afterward?
items.answer: The free trial runs 14 days and includes 500 credits for Search, Research and scoring.

sections.heading: About the challenge

items.question: What makes a search a good fit for the challenge?
items.answer: A kind of US business you can describe in plain words, a geography, and the traits that separate a great match from an ordinary one. The harder it is to find in a prospect database, the better.

items.answer: We read every search and take the ones Scorecard can run well today. If yours isn’t one of them, we’ll tell you why.

items.question: What do you ask in return?

sections.heading: A list tells you who exists. It doesn’t tell you who deserves your time.
sections.body: Finding another thousand company names isn’t the hard part of proprietary search. Applying your judgment to every one of them, the same way, is.

items.label: 01 · Thesis fit
items.title: Who actually matches the thesis?
items.body: Not just the industry code: the business model, the customers, the way the company runs.

items.label: 02 · Research
items.title: Who deserves a closer look?
items.body: Which companies are worth deeper work before anyone reaches out.

items.label: 03 · Attention
items.title: Who gets the handwritten letter?
items.body: Which owners are worth personal outreach and months of patient follow-up.

sections.heading: Your thesis, turned into a score.
sections.body: Scorecard makes the judgment calls in your buy box explicit, checks the public evidence for each company, and ranks every one against the same standard.

items.label: 01 · Define
items.title: Write down the thesis
items.body: Your target profile, must-haves and red flags, in plain language. Each one becomes a Signal Scorecard checks.

items.label: 02 · Score
items.title: Score the market
items.body: Scorecard researches every matching company and scores it, with the source behind each finding.

items.label: 03 · Prioritize
items.title: Spend attention where it counts
items.body: Separate personal targets from broader outreach, the research queue, and the companies to drop.

sections.heading: Signals worth checking.
sections.body: Signals are the questions Scorecard answers for every company. Use the standard ones, or add the detail only you know matters.

items.title: Little digital presence
items.body: Can point to an overlooked, referral-driven operator with room to professionalize.

items.title: Multiple locations
items.body: Suggests operating scale, route density and a branch model that repeats.

items.title: Recurring commercial work
items.body: Maintenance programs and property-manager customers suggest repeat revenue.

items.title: Management beyond the owner
items.body: Branch managers, estimators and crew leads can mean less dependence on the owner.

items.title: Your own Signal
items.body: Ask your own question, like “Do they serve HOAs?”, and get an answer with its source for every company.

items.title: Unknown stays unknown
items.body: Willingness to sell isn’t in any public record. Scorecard marks it unknown instead of guessing.

sections.heading: Not every owner should get the same outreach.
sections.body: A grade turns the score into a decision about how much effort each company gets.

items.label: A
items.title: Personal campaign
items.body: Deep research, a personal letter, direct calls and long-term follow-up.

items.label: B
items.title: High-touch outreach
items.body: Personalized outreach across channels, with a set follow-up cadence.

items.label: C
items.title: Test the segment
items.body: Lower-cost outreach to test the segment and learn more.

items.label: D
items.title: Hold or drop
items.body: Poor fit, too little evidence, the wrong model, or a franchise or subsidiary.

sections.heading: Use Scorecard when your list still leaves too much work.
sections.body: Databases give you a broad universe. Scorecard helps when your real buy box depends on business model, customer mix, local presence or owner dynamics that filters miss.

items.label: Map the market
items.title: Build a market you can work
items.body: One consistent screen across every company in your geography, instead of another raw export.

items.label: Remove the lookalikes
items.title: Separate real fits from near misses
items.body: Commercial maintenance from residential projects, service from installation, independents from franchises.

items.label: Find the few
items.title: Pick the owners worth pursuing
items.body: The handful of companies that justify a tailored letter, a direct call and months of follow-up.

sections.heading: Questions from searchers

items.question: Does Scorecard know which owners want to sell?
items.answer: No, and nothing public does. Scorecard shows owner names and founding dates where public records and websites have them, and marks willingness to sell as unknown.

items.question: Which industries and geographies work?
items.answer: Any kind of US business you can describe in plain words. Coverage is strongest where companies have a web presence.

sections.heading: Privacy Policy

children.text: This policy explains what information [Scorecard legal entity name] ("Scorecard", "we", "us") collects through scorecardgtm.com (the "site") and the Scorecard app at app.scorecardgtm.com (the "service"), how we use it, and the choices you have. If you have questions, email support@scorecardgtm.com.
Information you give us
Forms on the site.

When you use the contact form or send us a search through the challenge form, we collect your name, email address, company (if you give it), and what you write: your message, or your search, geography and criteria.
Your account.
When you sign up for the service, we collect your name, email address and sign-in details.
What you put into the service.
The searches you run, the criteria and Signals you define, lists you upload, and notes you add.
Billing.
If you subscribe, our payment processor, [payment processor], collects your payment details. We don't store full card numbers.
Messages.
If you email us, we keep the email and our reply.
Information we collect automatically
Analytics and session recordings.

We use PostHog to understand how people use the site: pages viewed, clicks, referring site, device and browser type, and approximate location derived from your IP address. PostHog also records sessions, a reconstruction of how the page looked and what was clicked, so we can find what's confusing. Text typed into form fields is masked and is not recorded. PostHog stores an identifier in your browser's cookies or local storage to recognize return visits.
Hosting and security logs.
The site runs on Cloudflare, which processes your IP address and request details to deliver pages and protect against abuse.
Fonts.
The site loads fonts from Google Fonts, so your browser sends your IP address to Google when it fetches them.
Information about businesses and the people who run them

Scorecard researches US businesses using public sources such as company websites, public records and business directories. Results can include business details and the names, roles and business contact details of owners and employees, as they appear in those sources. We use this information only to provide the service: to help customers find, research and prioritize businesses. If you appear in our results and want your information corrected or removed, email support@scorecardgtm.com and we'll handle it promptly.
[Confirm the sources used, and whether contact details (email, phone) are included.]
How we use information
To run, maintain and improve the site and the service.
To answer your messages and to process challenge searches you send us.
To send service emails, such as sign-in links, account notices and replies to your messages. We send these through Cloudflare Email Sending.
To understand usage and fix problems.
To prevent fraud and abuse, and to meet legal obligations.
We don't sell personal information, and we don't share it for cross-context behavioral advertising.
Who we share it with
We share information only with service providers that help us run Scorecard, under agreements that limit their use of it:
Cloudflare
: website hosting, database, file storage and email sending.
PostHog
: product analytics and session recordings.
Google
: email (Google Workspace) and web fonts.
Vercel
: hosting for the Scorecard app.
[Payment processor]
: billing.
[AI and data providers]
: research and analysis performed by the service. [List the providers that receive search inputs.]
We may also disclose information if the law requires it, to protect the rights and safety of Scorecard or others, or as part of a merger, acquisition or sale of assets.
How long we keep it

We keep form submissions and messages for as long as we need them to respond and follow up, and for up to [24 months] after that. We keep account data while your account is open, and for up to [90 days] after you close it, unless the law requires longer. Analytics data is kept according to PostHog's retention settings, currently [retention period].
Your choices and rights
Access, correction and deletion.
Email support@scorecardgtm.com and we'll help. We may need to verify your identity first.
Analytics.
You can block PostHog with your browser's tracking protection or an ad blocker. The site still works.
Email.
Service emails are necessary to run your account. We don't send marketing email without your permission.
California residents
have the right to know what personal information we collect, to ask us to delete or correct it, and to not be discriminated against for using these rights. [Confirm whether CCPA thresholds apply.]
If you're in the EU, the UK or another region with data-protection laws

, you may have additional rights, including the right to object to processing and to complain to your local data-protection authority. [Confirm the legal bases and international transfer mechanism if serving these regions.]
Security
We use service providers with strong security practices, encrypt data in transit, and limit access to the people who need it. No system is perfectly secure, so we can't guarantee absolute security.
Children
Scorecard is a business tool and isn't directed to anyone under 16. We don't knowingly collect information from children.
Changes
If we change this policy, we'll update the date at the top, and for significant changes we'll let account holders know by email.
Contact

sections.heading: Terms of Service

children.text: These terms govern your use of scorecardgtm.com and the Scorecard app at app.scorecardgtm.com (together, the "service"), provided by [Scorecard legal entity name] ("Scorecard", "we", "us"). By creating an account or using the service, you agree to these terms. If you use Scorecard for a company, you agree on its behalf and confirm you're authorized to do so.
The service

Scorecard helps you find, research and rank businesses. You describe the companies you want, and Scorecard searches public sources, checks the criteria you set, and scores what it finds. We may change, add or remove features over time.
Accounts

You need an account to use the app. Keep your sign-in details secure and tell us at support@scorecardgtm.com if you think someone else has accessed your account. You're responsible for activity under your account. You must be at least 18 to use Scorecard.
Free trial, plans and payment
Free trial.
New accounts get a free trial of [14 days] with [500 credits]. [Confirm whether a card is required, and what happens when the trial ends.]
Monthly plan.
The monthly plan costs [$59 per month] plus applicable taxes. It renews automatically each month until you cancel.
Credits.
Searches, research and scoring use credits. Unused credits [expire at the end of each billing period / roll over]. Credits have no cash value. [Confirm credit rules.]
Cancellation.
You can cancel at any time. You keep access until the end of the period you've paid for. Except where the law requires otherwise, payments are non-refundable.
Price changes.
We'll give you at least 30 days' notice of a price change. It applies from your next renewal after the notice.
The challenge offer

When we offer to run a search for you through the challenge page, we choose which searches to accept. An accepted search may be free, in exchange for honest feedback on the results. Results are delivered by email and may include fewer companies than requested when the evidence supports fewer. The offer can end at any time.
How you may use Scorecard
You may use the service and its results for your own business purposes, such as prospecting, market research and acquisition search. You agree not to:

break any law while using the service or its results, including anti-spam, telemarketing, privacy and data-protection laws (for example CAN-SPAM, the TCPA and state privacy laws) when you contact businesses or people found through Scorecard;
resell, publish or redistribute results or data from the service as a list or database product;
scrape, copy or bulk-download the service by automated means, except through features we provide for that purpose;
try to get around usage limits, security measures or credit accounting;
use the service to harass anyone or to discriminate unlawfully;
reverse-engineer the service, or use it to build a competing product.
We may suspend or close accounts that break these rules.
Accuracy of results

Scorecard's research comes from public sources and automated analysis. It can be incomplete, out of date or wrong. Each finding shows its source so you can check it, and information we can't find is marked unknown. Check anything important before you rely on it. Scorecard doesn't tell you whether a business owner wants to sell, and nothing in the service is legal, financial or investment advice.
Your content

You own what you put into Scorecard: your searches, criteria, uploaded lists and notes ("your content"). You give us permission to use your content to provide and improve the service for you. We don't share your content with other customers. If you send us feedback or suggestions, we may use them without any obligation to you.
Our property

The service, including its software, design, scores and the way results are compiled, belongs to Scorecard and its licensors. These terms give you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the service while your account is active.
Third-party services
Scorecard relies on third-party services, such as hosting, email and payment providers. Your use of a third-party service directly is governed by that provider's terms.
Ending your use

You can stop using Scorecard and close your account at any time. We may suspend or end your access if you break these terms, if we're required to by law, or if we stop offering the service. If we end the service for reasons other than your breach, we'll refund any prepaid fees for the unused period.
Disclaimers

The service is provided "as is" and "as available". To the extent the law allows, we disclaim all warranties, whether express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement. We don't promise the service will be uninterrupted or error-free.

Our total liability for any claim relating to the service is limited to the greater of the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the claim and $100.
Indemnity

You agree to defend and indemnify Scorecard against claims arising from your use of the service or its results in breach of these terms or the law, including claims about how you contacted businesses or people found through Scorecard.
Changes to these terms
We may update these terms. If a change is significant, we'll tell account holders by email at least 30 days before it takes effect. If you keep using the service after that, you accept the new terms.
